Jordan / Kim / Anya —

I pulled the hourly breakdown and a 5k-line log extract; attaching the sampling_report.csv and log_extract_20260723.jsonl. Summary of findings (high-level):

- Between 2026-06-22 02:00 UTC and 2026-06-22 03:10 UTC we observed a burst of ~2.3M tokens labeled under namespace "cloudscale_prod" that correlate with a service migration job CloudScale ran on 2026-06-22 (we can see matching user-agent strings in the logs).
- The token attribution logic had a fallback that, for a short window during a key rotation, prefers an API key namespace embedded in a legacy header if tenant tagging is absent. In this case the migration job used the legacy header, and because of an overlap in API-key-to-namespace mapping created during rotation, ~18% of that jobs traffic was attributed to "cloudscale_prod" rather than "cloudscale_staging".
- Evidence files attached: sampling_report.csv (aggregate by tenant and hour) and log_extract_20260723.jsonl (redacted request_id, tenant_namespace, api_key_id, timestamp, user_agent).

Recommendation: apply a provisional credit of $18,400 to the disputed line (same amount shown on invoice_June2026.pdf) and mark a ticket for a codepath fix that ensures the legacy-header fallback is disabled during key rotations. I can draft the credit memo language if we agree.

Anya — if you want us to apply the provisional credit immediately we can do that and then reconcile after the RCA lands (ETA: ~2 business days for the full fix/PR).

—Ben
Ben Carter
Billing Operations Manager, Redwood Inference
